item.text:
Node and Python are both available. Since the repo is a blank slate, I'll build a self-contained, zero-dependency project. Here's my idea:

**A tiny "ASCII field generator" + live terminal simulator** — a single-page web toy that draws a scrolling ASCII landscape in your terminal, with a friendly command palette (help, theme, speed, even a little stats view). It's self-contained: one HTML file, no build step, no dependencies.

Let me plan the work:

items.text: Build the ASCII scene renderer and terminal UI

item.text: Now I'll create the project. First, the folder structure and README:

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "mkdir -p ascii-terminal && cat > ascii-terminal/README.md << 'EOF'
# ascii-terminal

A tiny, zero-dependency ASCII landscape generator that renders a scrolling
night-time scene in a fake terminal. Built with plain HTML, CSS, and
JavaScript — no build step, no frameworks, no external assets.

## Run it

Open "'`index.html` in a browser, or serve the folder locally:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory ascii-terminal
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `help` | Show available commands |
| `speed <1-10>` | Change the scroll speed |
| `theme <name>` | Switch color scheme (`night`, `amber`, `matrix`, `paper`) |
| `clear` | Clear the scrollback buffer |
| `about` | Show a little blurb |
| `quit` | Stop the animation (well, "quit" — you'"'ll come back) |

You can also press "'`?` to see the command list, or just hit `Enter` with an
empty line to start/pause the scene.
EOF
echo done'

All wired correctly: `theme: night`, `speed: 5`, `rows: 24`, `state: running`, body class `theme-night`.

Now let me verify command dispatch works end-to-end. I'll expose the command handler by simulating keydown on `cmdEl`:

I found a real bug: `renderRows()` sets `screenEl.textContent`, which wipes the scrollback/help text every frame — that's why my command test showed nothing but the ground line. The scene and scrollback can't share one element.

I'll fix the architecture: an animated scene layer behind a transparent scrollback layer. Let me update the HTML/CSS/JS accordingly.

item.aggregated_output: HTML/CSS updated

item.text: Now update the JS to target `#scene` for the animated render and `#scrollback` for the command output:

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cd /workspace/ascii-terminal && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
html = open('index.html').read()

# JS top: reference scene element
old = '''  const screenEl = document.getElementById(\"screen\");
  const cmdEl = document.getElementById(\"cmd\");'''
new = '''  const sceneEl = document.getElementById(\"scene\");
  const scrollEl = document.getElementById(\"scrollback\");
  const cmdEl = document.getElementById(\"cmd\");'''
assert old in html
html = html.replace(old, new)

# renderRows sets scene text
old = '''    screenEl.textContent = rows.map((r) => r.join(\"\")).join(\"\\\\n\");
  }'''
new = '''    sceneEl.textContent = rows.map((r) => r.join(\"\")).join(\"\\\\n\");
  }'''
assert old in html
html = html.replace(old, new)

# scrollback element references
html = html.replace(\"screenEl.appendChild(div);\", \"scrollEl.appendChild(div);\")
html = html.replace(\"screenEl.removeChild(screenEl.firstElementChild);\", \"scrollEl.removeChild(scrollEl.firstElementChild);\")
html = html.replace(\"screenEl.childElementCount > 600\", \"scrollEl.childElementCount > 600\")
html = html.replace(\"screenEl.innerHTML = \\\"\\\"; appendRow(\\\"scrollback cleared\\\");\", \"scrollEl.innerHTML = \\\"\\\"; appendRow(\\\"scrollback cleared\\\");\")

item.text:
Done! Since the repo was a blank slate, I built a small self-contained toy: **ascii-terminal** — a scrolling ASCII landscape rendered in a fake terminal.

**What's in it**
- `ascii-terminal/index.html` — the whole app in one file (HTML/CSS/JS, zero dependencies)
- `ascii-terminal/README.md` — run instructions and command reference

**How it works**
- A night scene with parallax layers: stars and clouds (slow), rolling hills (medium), and foreground bushes/rocks (fast), plus a fixed moon and a drawn ground line
- A live scrollback terminal with a prompt and status bar

**Commands**
- `help` / `?`, `about`, `clear`
- `speed <1-10>` — scroll speed
- `theme <night|amber|matrix|paper>` — color schemes
- `quit` — pause; empty line toggles run/pause

**Verification**
- `node --check` passes on the extracted script
- Headless functional tests confirmed: scene renders and advances each frame, commands update the status bar, themes switch `body` classes, and state toggles work

**To run it**
```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory ascii-terminal
# open http://localhost:8000
```
or just open `ascii-terminal/index.html` directly. I couldn't start a live server here because the sandbox blocks sockets, but it's a static page so it opens fine in any browser.
